instruction: Advise on wire-EDM quality / surface integrity for the following.
input: Taper accuracy: skim passes are critical
output: Taper dimensional accuracy is WORSE than straight cuts by a factor of 1.5-2×. The wire deflects differently at angles, and the offset compensation must account for the angled kerf geometry. Always run at least 2 skim passes on taper cuts (vs 1 that might suffice for straight cuts). On the skim passes, disable taper offset compensation (H=0.0000) as shown in the NOZE TEST program — the skim passes follow the same UV path as the rough cut.

instruction: Share the JM Die shop-floor wire-EDM practice for the following.
input: JM Die M-code usage frequency — M30 is RARE (10%) on FA-10S; M02 is canonical program-end (100%)
output: Empirical M-code usage from JM Die WIRE EDM archive (JM_DIE_MCODE_USAGE in jm-die-wedm-program-patterns.ts). Per-program usage percentages: M78 fill-tank / M80 water-on / M82 wire-on / M84 power-on / M02 program-end ALL run at 100% (universal start + end essentials). M90 adaptive-ON / M91 adaptive-OFF = 95% (the 5% misses are tiny test programs without adaptive). M20 thread-wire / M21 cut-wire = 90% (multi-cutout programs use them; single-cutout simple programs sometimes skip auto-thread). M85 power-off / M83 wire-off / M81 fluid-off / M58 drain-tank = 85% (some programs leave tank filled for the next job). M01 optional-stop (glue-stop) = 70% (multi-profile programs use them; single-profile skip). **M30 is RARE at only 10% usage** — JM Die's canonical program-end is M02, NOT M30. CAM posts / AI generators that emit M30 instead of M02 on FA-10S still work but break the shop's grep-based audit tooling that searches for M02 to identify program tails. Wizard rule: emit M02 (not M30) on FA-10S-targeted programs.

instruction: Share the JM Die shop-floor wire-EDM practice for the following.
input: JM Die FA-10S M-code start sequence — M91→M20→M78→M80→M82→M84→M90 (double M78 tank fill, M90 rough only)
output: Ground truth from all 4 JM Die FA-10S production programs (ITW SHAKEPROOF, NOZE TEST, CHOCTAW DEFENSE, FIOCCHI). The shop-canonical M-code start-of-cut sequence (before EACH cutout in a multi-cutout fixture) is 7 codes in fixed order: M91 (adaptive-control OFF init) → M20 (reset/clear) → M78 (open/fill — first issue) → M80 (wire feed on) → M82 (high-pressure flush on) → M84 (wire tension on) → M90 (adaptive-control ON for rough cut). End-of-cut sequence: M85 (wire tension off) → M83 (high-pressure flush off) → M81 (wire feed off) → M21 (cycle stop) → M58 (return). Tank fill is ALWAYS double M78 M78 (operator-shipped pattern — single M78 was observed to fail tank-fill detection on FA-10S firmware ~rev 1996-2002). Adaptive control discipline: M90 ON for rough pass only, M91 OFF for ALL skim passes — adaptive servo overshoots on light skim cuts and causes inconsistent kerf. Glue stop between cutouts is M01 (operator-confirmable pause). Program end is M02. CRITICAL: a hand-written or AI-generated FA-10S program that emits only M78 once (no double), or that emits M90 on a skim pass, will run but produce inferior surface finish + variable kerf — recognize these as program-quality smell tests.

instruction: Provide wire-EDM setup guidance for the following.
input: Workpiece leveling: tram to <0.01mm across full length
output: Before wire cutting, tram the workpiece surface to within 0.01mm across its full length using a dial indicator on the machine's edge finder. An un-level workpiece means the wire path is not perpendicular to the surface — the cut will have an unintended taper. For parts longer than 200mm, check at 3+ points. Magnetic chucks can warp thin parts — use parallels underneath to support the span.

instruction: Share the JM Die shop-floor wire-EDM practice for the following.
input: JM Die E-code family distribution — 60% standard 4-pass / 25% heavy 5-pass / 10% UV taper / 3% E952 / 2% E56xx
output: Empirical E-code family distribution at JM Die WIRE EDM (from JM_DIE_ECODE_FAMILY_DISTRIBUTION in jm-die-wedm-program-patterns.ts): E12xx_standard_4pass = 60% (the workhorse — D2/A2/S7/M2/H13/4140/4340/O1/W1 standard dies + punches). E12xx_heavy_5pass = 25% (cannelure / thick stock / hardened steel >15mm). E28xx_taper_5pass = 10% (taper dies + UV-axis precision work). E952_acu_7pass_thin = 3% (precision 7-pass cycle for thin / fine-feature work — Mitsubishi 'acu' family for ultra-precision). E56xx_acu_7pass_thick = 2% (precision 7-pass for thick stock — same 'acu' lineage, different generator energy curve). Wizard / AI default proposal rule: when the operator submits a job without constraints, propose E12xx_standard_4pass first (60% probability of being right). When a print specifies Ra < 0.4 µm OR positional tolerance < ±0.0001", reach for the 7-pass acu families (E952 thin / E56xx thick) — these are the ONLY families that hit that quality envelope.

instruction: Advise on the wire-EDM machining practice below.
input: Maximum taper angle depends on workpiece thickness
output: WEDM taper is limited by the machine's UV travel and the distance between upper and lower guides. Maximum taper angle = atan(UV_max_travel / guide_gap). For a typical Mitsubishi FA20S with ±30mm UV travel and 350mm guide gap: max taper ≈ ±5°. For larger tapers, reduce the guide gap by raising the lower guide. WARNING: reducing guide gap below 100mm + workpiece thickness risks collision. Always verify clearance with dry run (G0 only, no wire).

instruction: Share the wire-EDM tactic for the following situation.
input: WEDM pass-count vs Ra vs recast cascade — 1-pass 50-150 µm recast, 4-6 pass <5 µm, 5-8 pass near-zero
output: Canonical pass-count → quality ladder from [[wedm-tactics-multipass-and-recast]] wiki (slot hotel U-WIKI-WEDM-MULTIPASS-RECAST, 2026-05-21). Match pass count to the spec; don't over-machine — every added skim costs cycle time. (1) Bulk separation, finish irrelevant: 1 pass rough only → Ra 2-5 µm, recast 50-150 µm. (2) Standard tolerance, moderate finish: 2 passes (rough + 1 skim) → Ra 1-2 µm, recast 20-50 µm. (3) Tight tolerance, good finish: 3 passes (rough + 2 skim) → Ra 0.4-1.0 µm, recast 5-20 µm. (4) Precision die/mold, mirror finish: 4-6 passes → Ra <0.4 µm, recast <5 µm. (5) Aerospace/medical, recast-controlled: 5-8 passes + verified cross-section → Ra <0.2 µm, near-zero recast. JM Die's E12xx standard 4-pass falls in tier (4) precision die. E12xx heavy 5-pass + E28xx taper 5-pass also tier (4). E952 / E56xx 7-pass cycles hit tier (5) aerospace-grade. Single-pass rough is NEVER used at JM Die (the test 'Wire Program - 5 inch square.NC' is the only 1-pass program — explicitly a training/test cut, not production).

instruction: Advise on the wire-EDM machining practice below.
input: JM Die A2 tool steel — slightly faster than D2, same offset cascade
output: A2 tool steel (1.0%C, 5%Cr, 1%Mo) cuts 10-15% faster than D2 on wire EDM due to lower chromium content reducing electrical resistance. At JM Die, A2 is used for larger punches and die shoes where toughness matters more than wear resistance. Use the same E12xx sequences and H-register offsets as D2, but feed rate can be increased — E1221 runs at ~2.3 in/min on 1" A2 vs 2.0 in/min on D2. The HAZ on A2 is slightly smaller, but still run 3+ skim passes. A2 is more prone to rust in the dielectric tank — run finish skims within 24 hours of roughing to avoid surface oxidation between passes.

instruction: Explain the wire-EDM ML / AI insight below.
input: Bayesian-optimized CNN-SVM for real-time surface classification
output: Hybrid Bayesian-optimized CNN-SVM model enables real-time surface roughness classification and prediction from in-process machined surface images. Bayesian optimization auto-tunes hyperparameters for both CNN feature extractor and SVM classifier. Achieves production-viable inference times for closed-loop quality control.

instruction: Share the wire-EDM tactic for the following situation.
input: WEDM wire-tension scales with part-height; skim passes run HIGHER tension than rough (counter-intuitive)
output: Wire-tension discipline from [[wedm-tactics-wire-and-flushing]] wiki (slot hotel U-WIKI-WEDM-WIRE-FLUSHING, 2026-05-21). Wire tension trades ACCURACY (high tension keeps wire straight under flushing+discharge force) vs BREAK-RISK (high tension fatigues the wire at the discharge zone where heat weakens it). Height-tiered envelope: (1) <25 mm part height — low-to-medium tension; short unsupported span, bow is small. (2) 25-100 mm — medium-to-high tension; span bows under flushing pressure, tension counters it. (3) >100 mm — HIGH tension + hard-brass wire (or coated); long span needs maximum straightness, plain brass at high tension may break — switch wire material. COUNTER-INTUITIVE RULE: skim passes run at HIGHER tension than the rough pass. Rough does most material removal at high discharge energy where break-risk is already elevated — keep tension medium to give thermal margin. Skim passes have low discharge energy (less wire heating) so they can SAFELY run high tension and PRIORITIZE the straightness/finish/recast-reduction objective. Mastercam WEDM posts that emit constant tension across all passes are wrong by this discipline; the operator typically dials tension up between rough and first skim at the machine.

instruction: Provide wire-EDM setup guidance for the following.
input: JM Die program shutdown sequence — M21-M85-M83-M81-M79 then M02
output: JM Die programs follow the standard Mitsubishi FA shutdown M-code sequence: M21 (cut wire at lower guide), M85 (power supply off), M83 (wire drive off), M81 (water circulation off), M79 (drain tank — optional for short jobs), then M02 or M30 (program end). The M21 wire cut command positions the wire end above the lower guide for easy re-threading. Never skip M85 before M83 — cutting wire drive with power still active can damage the wire feeder. For multi-start hole programs, omit M79 drain until after all profiles are complete. The neural analysis engine flags 'AP007: No program end M02/M30' as a major anti-pattern.

instruction: Explain the wire-EDM AI optimization insight below.
input: Taguchi DOE is most effective for WEDM parameter optimization — reduces trials by 80%
output: Taguchi Design of Experiments (DOE) and ANOVA are the most effective techniques for determining optimal WEDM process variables. Taguchi DOE is straightforward, efficient, and reduces the number of trials by up to 80% compared to full factorial experiments while maintaining quality.

instruction: As a wire-EDM CNC programming expert, explain the following programming practice.
input: Makino DUO: use line-only lead-in; never arc leads on taper programs
output: Makino application notes (embedded in Mastercam Makino 4X Wire TECH.pst) explicitly state: use line-only lead-in and lead-out geometry. Arc leads create compensation discontinuities at the G40→G41/G42 switch point, causing dimension errors at the entry point. For taper programs: when cutting a feature with a land (constant-height zone in a tapered profile), always set the chain height to the land height. The Makino post outputs this as the P value (program plane) and Q (opposite taper end). The P value is the reference dimension-holding surface — incorrect chain height will shift the final dimension to the wrong Z level.

instruction: Advise on wire-EDM speeds/feeds for the situation below.
input: Finishing pass wire speed affects Ra consistency
output: During finishing (skim) passes, maintain wire speed at 6-8 m/min for best Ra consistency. Lower wire speed causes the same wire section to receive multiple discharges, creating thermal fatigue marks. Higher speed wastes wire. The wire speed does NOT affect cutting speed — it only affects the wire surface condition presented to the discharge gap. For roughing, wire speed of 10-12 m/min is standard to prevent wire breakage from thermal accumulation.

instruction: Give the JM Die FA-10S shop-calibrated settings for one pass of a wire-EDM cut.
input: Family: 4-axis UV taper, 5-pass — stainless/taper die pattern. Pass 4 of 5 (skim).
output: Pass 4 (skim): E-code E2824, feed 0.3 ipm (7.62 mm/min), H4 wire offset 0 in (0 mm). Skim pass — adaptive control M91 (off); reduce flush pressure vs the rough pass.
